problems: Minor (non-blocking) caveat: the page relies on the UA keyboard-focus ring being a 1px dotted black line. WCAG F78 itself frames the focus ring this way, but modern Chromium draws a solid dark focus ring rather than the historic dotted one. On strict modern-Chrome rendering the focus ring may be solid (not dotted), which would make the focused link slightly distinguishable from the dotted-only siblings. The fixture's F78 mode-2 mechanism (resting decoration identical to the technique's documented focus-indicator style) is still exactly what the cited technique codifies, so the documented 'failed' outcome holds; the rendered visual identity is just UA-dependent in degree.

Minor (non-defect) caveat: in the focused text-input screenshot the one visible change is the native text caret, not the focus indicator the SC concerns; for the select and date controls there is no caret, so for those controls the resting->focused appearance is even more identical. Does not affect the verdict.

Inspect tool tab-order expanded the date input into multiple spin-button stops (stops 3-6 all id 'pickup') and shows FOCUSED computed styles for form controls; this is a tool rendering nuance, not a page defect.

PROMPT/HARNESS METADATA MISMATCH (not a file defect): the prompt's Claimed scenario describes a 'Legal Master Services Agreement' page with selector '.clause-refs a', but the actual case-03.html/.md is a Payments API reference page with selector '.endpoints a'. The .html and .md are internally consistent with each other; I evaluated the real file and ran inspect.js against the real selector '.endpoints a'.

Minor fidelity note (not a defect): F78's example uses 'border: medium solid black' relying on the UA default ring drawn outside a border, whereas this fixture forces the equivalent via an explicit author rule '.endpoints a:focus { outline:2px solid #000; outline-offset:1px }' (same black, thinner than the 4px border). The .md/.html explicitly call this out as making the failure deterministic — a faithful adaptation of F78 mode 3, not a misattribution.

Task-prompt 'Claimed scenario' is stale/inconsistent with the actual artifact: it says '5px solid navy' border and a custom 'outline:2px solid #1b2a4a' ring, but the real page (HTML lines 60, 80-83) uses an 8px navy border and a 'box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #1b2a4a' ring with outline:none. The actual HTML and the .md doc are mutually consistent and sound; only the orchestrator's summary diverges. I judged the real artifact, which is valid.

Minor over-statement of automated blindness: a focused-vs-unfocused screenshot pixel-diff would register a non-zero change at the outer edge (the 1px box-shadow does paint), so 'no scanner can flag a diff' is technically true only for the same-hue PERCEPTUAL distinguishability, not raw pixel change. The doc itself acknowledges this nuance (diff is non-zero), so it is not a defect, just worth noting.

Minor framing nit (not a substantive defect): the page/doc repeatedly assert that 'axe-core, WAVE and Lighthouse pass 2.4.7'. More precisely, these tools have no focus-visibility rule at all and simply do not cover SC 2.4.7 (axe-core in particular ships no 2.4.7 rule), so they neither pass nor fail it. The human-judgment claim itself remains valid.

Tab-order signal contains expected UA noise, not a page defect: input[type=date] expands into several internal Chromium spin-button stops (id='start' repeated, stops 3-6) and a shadow-DOM 'Show date picker' button at stop 6 reports outlineStyle:none. That sub-button is UA shadow content, not the author control under test; the author date field itself carries the same 2px #1a1a1a outline as the other controls. No action needed.
No defects found. This is a correctly-labeled PASSED boundary case (not a failure). The documented passing mechanism is real and accurate.

Minor citation grep note (not a defect): the WCAG Understanding quote is split across two lines in the source (lines 25-26 of wcag-understanding/focus-visible.html), so a single-line grep misses it, but the sentence appears VERBATIM allowing only line-wrap whitespace differences. Trusted Tester quote matches verbatim at line 22 of refs/trusted-tester/sc-2.4.7-focus-visible.md. Both citations valid and support the claim.

Minor framing imprecision (not a defect): the doc leads with G195's 'area / 4 CSS px shortest side' argument (check #3), but the cleaner and decisive failure is checks #4 (contrast change >=3:1) and #5 (>=2px thick if <3:1). The 1px #f7f7f7 ring is ~1.09:1 and only 1px, so #4 and #5 both fail and G195's Expected Result ('Checks #2, #4, and #5 are true') is not met. The verdict (failed) is correct regardless; only the emphasis on the area limb is slightly looser than the contrast/thickness limb.
Contrast value: rounded ~1.09:1 by sRGB luminance vs the doc's stated ~1.07:1 — negligible difference; both are far below 3:1 and the maxChannelDelta=8/255 (#f7f7f7 vs #ffffff) is exactly correct.

Minor descriptive imprecision (does NOT change the outcome): the HTML comment (lines 14-16, 33) and the .md (lines 25, 30) attribute the per-gap math to '17px'/'@16px', but the nav.cats links actually render at fontSize 12.8px (the .8rem at the 16px root). The body is 17px but the nav is not. The LIVE-measured figures in the doc are nonetheless correct (Antipasti 81.98px->83.36px, ~0.17px/gap matches my measurement exactly), so the failure magnitude and outcome label are unaffected; only the font-size attribution is loose.
The base letter-spacing on nav.cats a is set twice (line 50 on nav.cats, line 60 on nav.cats a) both to .12em; harmless redundancy, not a defect.

Internal inconsistency in source: HTML CSS comment (line 66) labels the ring '~4.9:1' while the .md doc and the actual computed value are 6.02:1 (#1763b5 vs #ffffff). The 6.02:1 figure is correct; the comment is stale/wrong. Cosmetic only, does not affect the PASS verdict.

This is a PASS/boundary anchor, not a defect page; 'errorIsReal' is interpreted as 'the documented accessibility characteristic (a genuinely perceptible, G195-clearing focus indicator) truly exists' — it does. There is no failure here by design.

Minor labeling nuance only (not a defect): F55 spans 2.1.1/2.4.7/2.4.13/3.2.1; this page sits at the boundary with 2.1.1 (focus cannot settle on the control) and 2.4.3, but the 2.4.7-specific reading (the valid .apply-btn:focus ring never paints because focus is relocated within a frame) is sound and is the dominant interpretation, so the SC 2.4.7 'failed' label is correct.

Observation (not a defect): the focus-bounce also disrupts traversal of the adjacent 'Save for later' link (puppeteer Tab probe shows BODY on every stop including where the link should sit), because Tab resumes from body[tabindex=-1] at document start; this strengthens, not weakens, the keyboard-defect claim.

Minor doc/observation mismatch (not a defect in the verdict): the doc claims 'Puppeteer Tab traversal shows Tab 1 landing directly on span#srch-status'. The inspect.js tab-order recorded stop 0 = srch-status and a later 'body/none' reset, and my own keyboard.Tab-from-body simulation first landed on a link (A), not the span. The focus-theft itself is real either way; the exact first-Tab landing element is harness/timing-dependent and the doc's specific 'Tab 1 -> srch-status' phrasing is not exactly reproducible. The cleanest proof is programmatic focus on #q.

No local reference file exists for the F55 technique in refs/ (only the Trusted Tester SC text is bundled); F55 had to be verified against the live W3C page. Both the F55 title and the quoted sentence were confirmed verbatim externally, so this is a sourcing note, not a hallucination.

Note: this is a PASS-boundary case (expected outcome = passed), not an accessibility error. 'errorIsReal' is interpreted as 'the documented claim is genuine' — the claim is that the page legitimately PASSES via SCR31 (not F55), and that claim is real and sound.

Minor framing nuance: the page would PASS on the native :focus outline alone (button.switch:focus { outline: 3px solid #ffd24a }, HTML line 56) even if the scripted SCR31 ring were absent. The .kbd-focus box-shadow is therefore redundant/decorative rather than load-bearing for the pass, so the doc's emphasis on SCR31 as 'the' indicator slightly over-attributes the pass to the script. Does NOT change the passed outcome.
Folder name 'script-removes-focus-on-receipt' is the F55 failing bucket; this is an intentional in-bucket PASS boundary (correct by design), but the case-label semantics differ from the folder name.

Minor scope note (not a defect): the same outline:none-without-replacement pattern is also on .reserve (line 74), which is outside the declared element-under-test selector 'nav.primary a' but is consistent with the documented mechanism; it broadens, not contradicts, the case.

page.hover in headless did not visibly toggle the #dcffff pill in my Puppeteer run (no real pointer move), but the CSS source unambiguously declares the hover/active rule at lines 48-52, so the pointer-bound feedback is genuinely present; this is a tooling artifact, not a page defect.

Minor framing note (not a defect): C15 is a WCAG *sufficient* technique (how-to-pass), not a failure technique. The page legitimately uses C15's Tests/Procedure to show checks #2/#3 (focus indicator changes color / is removed on blur) would be FALSE here, and pairs it with C45 for the keyboard-vs-pointer nuance. Acceptable, but the case rests on absence-of-a-sufficient-technique rather than a dedicated failure technique like F78.

Citation precision (minor): the prompt-named citation F55 is verbatim ('the system focus indicator is an important part of accessibility for keyboard users.', F55.html lines 27-31) but F55's actual failure condition is script REMOVING focus via this.blur() (its 3 examples are all onFocus=this.blur()). This page never blurs focus; focus is retained, only the visible INDICATOR is absent. So F55 is thematically adjacent, not the tightest fit for this exact mechanism. The doc compensates by also citing C45 ('...browsers always show these styles when a user is navigating using the keyboard, but will generally not show them as a result of a mouse/pointer interaction...', C45.html line 22 verbatim), which is precisely on-point. Both quotes are genuine, not hallucinated.

The C45 reference file has an empty

(no literal 'C45' string inside), though the file path wcag-techniques/css/C45.html resolves and the title matches; not a defect, just noted.

Citation nuance (minor, not fatal): the C45 Procedure quote verifies VERBATIM (C45.html lines 68-71) but C45 step 2 ('Verify that once the component has received focus, a focus indicator is visible') read literally applies to the focused COMPONENT (the input), which DOES show a :focus border (rgb(37,99,235), confirmed in tabOrder). The .md correctly flags this as 'interpreted at the active-descendant level' — a defensible expert interpretation, but C45 alone is not the cleanest anchor for an activedescendant widget. The understanding-2.4.7 intent quote (focus-visible.html line 29, also verbatim) is the stronger support.

ACT rule id referenced in the .md (oj04fd) is used loosely ('interpreted at the active-descendant level') rather than as a direct mapping; oj04fd targets the focused element's indicator, so the mapping again relies on the activedescendant interpretation rather than literal rule application.

Minor citation nuance (not a defect): the C40 quote in the .md is literally about `box-shadow`, not gradients/background-images. The page uses a CSS linear-gradient, not box-shadow, so C40's verbatim sentence does not name the failing property. The .md is honest about this — it explicitly extends C40 by analogy in parentheses and the forced-colors gradient-suppression claim is independently correct per the CSS forced-colors spec. The task's named citation (G165) is verbatim and directly on point, so overall support stands.

By design the default render passes oj04fd (the gradient is a real pixel change); the failure only manifests in forced-colors mode, which the inspect tool / default light-mode render cannot directly show. The forced-colors flattening is inferred from spec rather than directly observed in the harness, but it is well-established UA behavior.

PROMPT METADATA MISMATCH (not a page defect): The prompt's claimed scenario/mechanism/selector describe a DIFFERENT case — a dark-theme 'TidalSync backup preferences' panel with native input/select/button using a background-IMAGE data: URI focus ring. The actual file is a light-theme 'Coastliner' rail seat-picker using CUSTOM div[role=button] widgets whose sole focus cue is a background-COLOR swap (#f3f5f9->#ffe08a) with outline:none. The prompt's element-under-test selector 'input[type=text]:focus, select:focus, button.save:focus' matches nothing in this file. I judged the actual page+doc, which are internally consistent.

Prompt's claimed citation lists only C40; the actual MD leads with G165 (more on-point) and uses C40's forced-colors note by explicit analogy (box-shadow -> background-color). Both quotes verify VERBATIM against wcag-techniques/general/G165.html line 4 and wcag-techniques/css/C40.html line 31. The C40-by-analogy framing is honestly flagged in the MD, not a misattribution.

Minor: under forced-colors the focused seat reports outlineColor rgba(0,230,255,0.8) (Chromium's would-be focus tint) but outlineStyle:none / outlineWidth:0px, so nothing is painted — inert value, does not rescue the cue. Confirms rather than weakens the failure.

Minor framing-only note (not a defect): the title/doc lean on three personas (magnifier off-screen, AT-invisible, forced-colors). The forced-colors strand is the weakest leg because with outline:none and no author-drawn box ON the star, forced-colors mode simply shows nothing on the star too — which is still a fail, but the 'author-drawn box divorced from element' wording in the .md (line 43) describes the corner marker, not anything on the star. The CORE mechanism (detached, AT-invisible, zero on-element change) is fully sound and is what carries the 'failed' verdict.

Minor/non-defect: the case is two-pronged (G165 AT-tracking failure + forced-colors flattening). Both are genuinely present and either alone supports 'failed', but the mechanism therefore straddles the 'drawn-indicator-fails-AT-tracking' and 'forced-colors' aspects rather than being a single clean aspect — worth noting for corpus distinctness/aspect-coverage bookkeeping, not a correctness problem.

inspect.js reported the target selector '.listbox:focus' as 'selector not found' because the static snapshot has no focused element; this is expected (CSS :focus rule exists in the stylesheet) and was confirmed via a scripted focus probe, not a page defect.
No real accessibility defect exists — this is intentionally a PASS case (md line 17 declares failure-mechanism: NONE; expected outcome 'passed'), so errorIsReal=false is by design, not a flaw.

Minor framing nuance: SC 2.4.7 is strictly about the default rendered state, where this page already passes outright via the box-shadow glow (the buttons get a visible white+blue ring on focus). The forced-colors robustness the case emphasizes is closer to 2-color-indicator / Focus Appearance (1.4.11/2.4.11) territory than to the bare 2.4.7 minimum. The 'passed' label is still correct for 2.4.7; the case's value rests on the contrastive forced-colors reasoning vs case-01, not on a 2.4.7-specific subtlety.

Because both case-06 (pass) and case-01 (fail) render an identical box-shadow ring in the default snapshot, a default-render automated checker would actually PASS BOTH. The human-judgment value is the contrastive/forced-colors distinction, which is legitimate but means the corpus must rely on the sibling pair to make the boundary meaningful.

Boundary classification: oj04fd's own Background section notes WCAG 2.0/2.1's 2.4.7 has no size/visibility threshold, so a surviving crescent is arguably 'some' visible change; the defect is most precisely 2.4.11 Focus Appearance / 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured. The 'failed' label is defensible under a human-judgment reading of 2.4.7 (indicator effectively unperceivable) but sits on a real SC boundary the doc could acknowledge more explicitly.

Mechanism depends on a fixed 1280px viewport: at the authored width the card right edge is x=999 and the ring overhangs to x=1018. At narrower widths the card shrinks but the translateX(13px) overhang is constant, so the clip relationship holds — verified non-fragile, but worth noting the geometry is width-anchored.

TASK-PROMPT MISMATCH (not a page defect, but flagged per instructions): the prompt's claimed scenario/mechanism/selector describe a DIFFERENT case than this file. Prompt claims a 'long-form news article with an in-article TOC', a position:sticky masthead (~135px), :target fragment navigation, selector '#policy:target', and mechanism 'targetTop=0 while stickyBottom=135, headingHiddenUnderSticky=true'. NONE of this is on the page: probe shows policyExists=false; .gov-bar is explicitly 'NOT sticky — ordinary document flow' (case-02.html L14-15); there is no TOC, no :target rule, no fragment navigation. The page's ACTUAL mechanism is focus({preventScroll:true}) on a below-fold field. The reviewer must judge the page on its own HTML+MD, which are internally consistent.

The selector supplied in the task prompt (#policy:target) does not exist in the file; the real element under test is #email (confirmed policyExists=false via probe). Verdict was assessed against the actual page content.

Minor citation-fit nuance (not a defect): the F78 quoted sentence lists examples about color/border SIMILARITY ('outlines that look the same as the focus outline', 'thick borders... same color as the focus indicator'), whereas this failure is geometric CLIPPING by overflow:hidden. The quote is verbatim (F78.html lines 29-31) and F78's broader description (line 27: indicator 'rendered non-visible by other styling on the page') fairly covers clip-based removal, so the citation is defensible but not a precise match to the listed examples.

Cosmetic: the inspect tool's `.tool:focus-visible` selector resolved to the 3rd button (U̲ تسطير, x=742) rather than the first; the geometry that proves the failure had to be measured with a direct Tab+boundingRect probe (first button focused: x=935→right=1023 vs toolbar clip right=981). This is a tool quirk, not a page defect.

Citation application is at the edge of F78's literal scope: F78's body and three examples address indicators that are turned off (outline:none), confusable with other outlines, or occluded by same-color borders — not clipping by an ancestor overflow/contain box. The quoted sentence DOES cover 'rendered non-visible by other styling,' and the partial clip of the ring's left/bottom rails + rounded corner is a reasonable application, but it is a borderline (partial-clip, not full-removal) reading rather than a textbook F78 example. This is acceptable for a human-judgment corpus but worth noting.

contain:paint is not strictly load-bearing for the failure — overflow:hidden alone fully accounts for the clip. The doc presents the two as stacked clip mechanisms (true), but a reader could over-credit contain:paint; the failure persists with overflow:hidden alone.

Selector under test '#cvc:focus-visible' is not statically matchable: the inspect.js querySelector returns 'selector not found' because :focus-visible only matches a keyboard-focused element. Not a page defect, but the selector cannot be resolved without live focus; live Puppeteer tabbing was required to confirm.

Minor naming nit: the case is labeled errorIsReal=false because it is a deliberate true-negative/PASS boundary variant (no accessibility error exists, by design); the 'passed' outcome label is the thing being verified and it is correct.
